newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures ignored the the negative impact of the truck drivers' strike on the French franc and followed Bunds and U.S. bond higher to settle within a whisker of the contract high reached last week.
The effect of the strike, now in its ninth day, was felt chiefly by the franc which slipped to a low of 3.3935 against the mark from a high of 3.3862.
Bond analysts said the long-end of the French curve remained relatively insulated from major upheaval as the bulk of bonds were held by domestic investors who needed to maintain long duration.
He said people outside France tended to be underweight in French assets or were holding short French positions already which would partly explain the lack of reaction by the bond market.

Some analysts said if the strike gets more widespread international media coverage in the coming days and a solution is not found soon, bonds could underperform from a further weakening of the currency.
"We could be in for some trouble," Iain Lindsay, bond analyst at Credit Lyonnais, said. "Even if it's solved today, are OATs really going to trade through Bunds?"
The 10-year spread between OATs and Bunds remained steady at parity late on Tuesday after moving briefly into positive territory early in the session.
March PIBOR slipped to a low of 96.34, down five basis points, but recovered to 96.37 even as the franc continued to weaken.
Some analysts said the slippage in the franc could end up being positive for PIBOR as it would lead to either a defence of the franc fort by monetary authorities or a cut in French interest rates.
